A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OMG-Bench dataset and HMATr framework. Their complete main text, appendices, equations, tables, and figures are readable and support comparison, including material relocated around the references.

before.justification: v1 reports original dataset statistics, HMATr evaluations on OMG-Bench and SHREC’21/22, component ablations, skeleton-quality experiments, and timing measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark and ablation results and adds annotation-agreement measurements, boundary-noise experiments, viewpoint comparisons, and confusion analysis.

M1.justification: The ST-GCN backbone, hierarchical FIFO memories, position-aware queries, matching and query-CTC losses, and non-overlapping inference procedure remain unchanged. Expanded explanations of collection and annotation do not establish a redesigned method.

E1.justification: OMG-Bench and SHREC’21/22 coverage remains unchanged. Section 9.2 extends the existing camera-0 skeleton-estimation tests to individual views 0–4, introducing viewpoint and severe self-occlusion scenarios within the retained dataset.

E2.justification: Table 3 adds AG-MAE as an evaluated baseline. OO-dMVMT also participates in the new boundary-noise and viewpoint comparisons. Existing main and macro-gesture comparator sets otherwise remain intact; the separate timing comparison disappears with v1 Table 14.

E3.justification: v2 adds joint annotation of 5% of the data, retraining with boundary noise of ±5 frames at p=0.5, and per-view inference. Section 8.3 changes Average Delay’s reference from gesture start to end. Section 10 replaces the stated noise augmentation with rotation/translation normalization; these reporting changes do not establish reruns of retained benchmarks.

E4.justification: The diagnostic evidence expands substantially: Section 7.2 tests annotation consistency and sensitivity to boundary noise, Section 9.2 examines viewpoint-dependent occlusion, and new Section 9.3 analyzes class confusion. These address annotation reliability and specific failure conditions beyond v1’s retained component ablations and camera-0 pose-estimator tests.

E5.justification: v2 introduces inter-annotator variability estimation using five experts jointly annotating 5% of the data, reporting mean boundary IoU of 0.81 and boundary variance reported as 2.13 frames. Neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests for recognition performance.

E6.justification: New findings cover annotation reliability, noise sensitivity, viewpoint robustness, and class confusion. Added results include AG-MAE’s 80.7% DR and noisy-boundary DRs of 89.1% for HMATr and 78.7% for OO-dMVMT. Conversely, v1 Table 14’s sequence-level timings, including HMATr’s 36.7 ms, disappear. Shared benchmark and ablation scores, including HMATr’s 89.2% DR, remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 8.3 revises the defined delay quantity by replacing the true gesture start with the true gesture end as its temporal reference. The model, memory-update, loss, and NLD equations otherwise retain their mathematical content; no new theorems or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same first-public-benchmark claim, HMATr contributions, and state-of-the-art performance claim. The advertised 7.6-percentage-point detection-rate advantage is unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 interprets boundary noise as having negligible training impact and attributes viewpoint results to robustness under occlusion and benefits of multi-view fusion. New confusion analysis identifies temporal single/double-tap ambiguity and coupled finger motion. The deployment explanation now attributes generalization to rotation/translation normalization instead of skeletal-noise augmentation.

D1.justification: v2 discloses baseline window size 16, stride 1, and logits threshold 0.8, and clarifies predefined-label assignment and expert corrections. It removes the code-in-supplement and pending-dataset-release statements and redirects the demo video to the project page. The PDFs do not establish an actual new code or dataset release.

R1.justification: v2 adds references including AG-MAE, MA-LMM, hierarchical multimodal consistency, and newer hand-pose/gesture work, while removing the 2019 path-signature/temporal-transformer gesture paper. Section 4.2 explicitly acknowledges prior inspiration for hierarchical memory, without substantially redefining the research positioning.

P1.justification: Targeted paragraph rewrites clarify data collection, memory motivation, and ablations; terminology and typos are corrected. Affiliations are expanded, acknowledgments are added, and references move before the supplementary material. The overall scientific narrative remains recognizable.

P2.justification: v2 adds the viewpoint bar chart and confusion matrix as Figures 7–8, removes Table 14, and adds an AG-MAE row to Table 3. It corrects table captions, resizes Figure 3, and reflows existing material; most retained visual designs are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The annotation-agreement and perturbation tests provide useful support for dataset reliability, while viewpoint testing, confusion analysis, and AG-MAE broaden scrutiny of the unchanged method. Clearer annotation and baseline details improve reproducibility. These gains are tempered by removal of sequence-level timing evidence and the unexplained delay-definition change despite unchanged reported delays, supporting a limited overall improvement.
